items.action: Patch ISE to 3.1P12 / 3.2P11 / 3.3P12 / 3.4P7 / 3.5P4 immediately. Check access.log for suspicious usernames (e.g. 'dummyuser') and re-image any compromised node from a known-good backup.
items.details: 77 new CVEs in Cisco's September batch, 41 in ISE (incl. a second CVSS 10.0, CVE-2026-76423) and 28 in Secure Firewall. No workarounds for the zero-day; iACLs on management traffic are interim mitigation.
items.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted API request to bypass Cisco Identity Services Engine's web management interface and gain root-level command execution. Cisco discovered it during a support case and confirms active exploitation; CISA added it to the KEV catalog with a September 19 deadline.
items.title: Cisco ISE zero-day (CVE-2026-76460, CVSS 10.0) under active exploitation

items.action: Review the vendor advisory, apply the recommended Jumbo Hotfix / LivePatch take for your release, and restrict management-plane exposure.
items.details: Affected: R82.20, R82.10 (Take 44 or earlier), R82 (Take 126 or earlier), R81.20 (Take 166 or earlier), plus older releases. Remediation via dedicated LivePatch takes — verify against Check Point's current Security Knowledge article.
items.summary: A critical flaw in Check Point Security Management, Multi-Domain Management, and Log Server deployments lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker reach root through the login mechanism itself.
items.title: Check Point management servers exposed to unauthenticated root RCE (CVE-2026-91843, CVSS 9.8)

items.action: Apply IBM's latest security update for Guardium Data Protection 12.2 and audit management-interface access logs for anomalous logins.
items.details: CWE-306 (missing authentication for critical function). No public exploit confirmed yet; EPSS rated low risk (0.43%) but severity warrants immediate patching.
items.summary: Disclosed September 18: an unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass IP-based access controls and reach the Guardium management interface.
items.title: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 auth bypass (CVE-2026-82967, CVSS 9.8)

items.action: Monitor for the group's IOCs and verify backup integrity if you do business with affected supply chains.
items.details: Double-extortion RaaS group using phishing plus Cobalt Strike, encrypting with the .ryshida extension and demanding Bitcoin. Listing reflects the group's claim; victim confirmation status unclear.
items.summary: Rhysida added Kreishandwerkerschaft Borken to its dark-web leak site on September 19, 2026 — the group's 283rd listed victim since June 2023.
items.title: Rhysida lists German professional-services firm Kreishandwerkerschaft Borken

items.details: AuditTeam has claimed 44 victims globally, using a double-extortion model. No verified details yet on stolen data or initial access; treat as an alleged claim rather than a confirmed breach.
items.summary: ThreatMon's team detected AuditTeam adding an Italian organization (identity partially obscured as 'tdup') to its leak site on September 19.
items.title: AuditTeam claims another victim (td***up, Italy) on September 19

items.action: If you hold a Revolut account, watch for phishing leveraging KYC data and enable all account alerts.
items.details: The group shared redacted screenshots and a screen recording of purported KYC documents (licences, passports, selfies, transaction histories). Revolut says it received no direct contact or demand and is supporting affected customers with law enforcement involved.
items.summary: A group calling itself 'iamnotavillain' posted a 24-hour countdown demanding 6,000 XMR (~$3M / ₹28.8 crore) for customer identity and transaction records it claims to hold from a breach affecting at least 680 Revolut accounts.
items.title: Hackers publicly demand $3M Monero ransom from Revolut over alleged breach

items.action: BFSI teams should join SOC telemetry with transaction logs, employee-access records, beneficiary graphs, and blockchain tracing in the first hours of any payment-fraud incident.
items.details: Proceeds were layered through 34 bank accounts; police have put ₹1.7 crore on hold. Investigators are examining a suspected Dubai connection, Telegram groups linked to Chinese actors, and conversion of some funds into USDT.
items.summary: Delhi Police's IFSO unit arrested five people — including a private-bank relationship manager — over a cyberattack on an NBFC that siphoned ~₹12.84 crore through 317 unauthorized digital transactions.
items.title: ₹12.84-crore NBFC cyber heist: Delhi Police IFSO arrests 5, including bank employee

items.action: Check bank statements regularly and disable UPI collect-request auto-approval; report unknown transactions to 1930 immediately.
items.details: Police are examining her iPhone, PhonePe account, UPI channel, and the bank account to determine the compromise vector — unauthorized device access is suspected but not yet established.
items.summary: The MLA's Union Bank of India account was hit by multiple unauthorized PhonePe and UPI transactions between August 22 and September 13, discovered on a bank statement September 14; FIR registered at Dhoomanganj, Prayagraj with cyber-cell assistance.
items.title: Chail MLA Pooja Pal flags ₹1.55 lakh in unauthorized PhonePe/UPI withdrawals

items.details: Police specifically warn against downloading APK files from unknown numbers; report cyber fraud via helpline 1930.
items.summary: Fraudsters are calling consumers claiming pending gas bills and threatening disconnection, then pushing APK downloads that give them access to the victim's device for unauthorized transactions.
items.title: Agra Police warn of 'gas bill' scam pushing malicious APKs
